recentItems.title: How to talk to your family about money | Anneleen Michiels | TEDxUHasselt
recentItems.description:
Money doesn’t break families. Silence does. 

In this TEDx talk, Anneleen challenges families, entrepreneurs and leaders to engage in the conversations about wealth they’ve been avoiding, and shows why avoidance, not disagreement, is the real risk.

Anneleen Michiels is a professor of finance who studies what happens when money and human relationships collide across generations. For over fifteen years, she has examined how wealth and ownership influence decision-making, conflict, and legacy in families and organizations worldwide. As the author of Money & Generations, Anneleen translates rigorous academic insight into ideas that change how people think and talk about money, responsibility, and the future. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why ‘Just Pick a Niche’ Is Bad Advice | Rani Peluso | TEDxAlmansorParkStudio
recentItems.description:
What if the reason you can't find your niche isn't a lack of clarity, but a lifetime of experience that doesn't fit neatly into one label? 

In this personal, humorous and emotional TEDx talk, business and mindset coach Rani Peluso shares how a devastating encounter with a mentor led her to question everything she knew about herself and how her unlikely background in computer programming helped her rediscover her confidence. 

Her story challenges conventional career and business advice, revealing why recognising the patterns in your own life may be more powerful than allowing someone else to decide who you should become. Rani Peluso is a business and mindset coach, author and founder of RANI COACHING, with more than 23 years of experience in coaching and personal development. She holds a BSc (Hons) in Science and Computing from London, UK, and spent 15 years working in investment banking before building her coaching business. 

An Advanced Demartini Method Facilitator, Rani has developed hundreds of personalised business blueprints helping coaches identify the unique intersection of their strengths, experiences and expertise. She is co-author of Elevate Your Mindset and author of the forthcoming Money. 

Mission. Meaning., and has shared her insights through radio, speaking engagements and educational workshops. Fascinated by human behaviour, technology and personal transformation, she explores how seemingly unrelated life experiences can reveal a person’s distinctive contribution. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Shaping the Future | Fiona Curran | TEDxSWA Youth
recentItems.description:
What can the past teach us about the future? Fiona invites us to reflect on how the world continues to evolve and the choices that shape what comes next. 

Her talk explores the relationship between change, innovation, and human responsibility, reminding us that the future is not simply something we wait for but something we help create. A Middle School and High School teacher at Sinarmas World Academy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Happy Ending หรรษาอยู่หนใด | Krip Longlong | TEDxTriam Udom Suksa Youth
recentItems.description:
⋆.˚🎭 หากเปรียบชีวิตคนเราให้เหมือนกับละคร ทุกคนก็คงคาดหวังให้ละครชีวิตของตัวเองจบลงด้วยความสุข แต่ถ้าชีวิตคือหนึ่งเรื่องละครจริง ๆ แล้ว 𝑯𝙖𝗽𝗽𝘆 𝒆𝗻𝗱𝙞𝗻𝒈 ของเราอยู่ตรงไหนกันแน่ . . อยู่ที่ตอนจบ หรืออยู่ที่ไหนสักแห่งระหว่างทาง ? 🛣️🎈. ݁₊ ⊹ 

‧⁺◟꒰👯🏻‍♀️ “หรรษา” กฤป ล่องหลง อดีตนักเรียนเตรียมอุดมศึกษา สาวผมสั้นที่เราน่าจะรู้จักกันดีในฐานะหอยจุ๊บ หวังหรือนักแสดงละครเวที 🥂𓂃꙳ ⋆

⁎⁺˳👩🏻‍🎨 เธอใช้ชีวิตของเธอไปกับการไขว่คว้าหาความสำเร็จตามความฝันที่ได้วาดจินตนาการไว้ ลองทำสิ่งต่าง ๆ มากมาย แต่เมื่อทำสำเร็จตามเป้าหมายที่ตั้งไว้ เธอกลับหันมาตั้งคำถามกับตัวเองเสมอว่า นี่คือความสุขของเราจริง ๆ หรือ ? 🔎💡 ໒꒱ ‧₊˚

₊˚⊹🌈 ชีวิตที่มัวแต่พุ่งไปหาเป้าหมายเพียงอย่างเดียว มันคือความสุขของเราจริง ๆ หรือเปล่า? Hunsa Krip Longlong — Triam Udom alumna, Face of Triam Udom, actress, and the face behind Hoi Jub Wang.

If life is a play, we all hope ours ends happily. But what if the Happy Ending isn’t waiting at the final curtain? What if it’s been hiding in the scenes in between all along?

Hunsa has spent her life chasing goals and dreams, only to reach them and ask herself the same quiet question: “Is this really what happiness feels like?”

Through stories of ambition, self-doubt, and learning to stay present, she explores how every life, like every play, is shaped not just by its ending — but by every role we choose, and every line we dare to rewrite.

Because the most important script is the one we write ourselves.
So, if your life were a play…
where would your Happy Ending be? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.description: Ce cred? Ce aleg? Ce fac? A.C.T ne ajută să oferim răspunsul la cele 3 întrebări, pentru a compune propria melodie în viață. recentItems.title: Seen it through ลองแลแบบละเลนส์ | Nitiwat Tantipatsiri | TEDxTriam Udom Suksa Youth
recentItems.description:
₊˚˖𓍢ִ🔎 เรากำลังไม่แน่ใจในสิ่งที่เราทำอยู่เพราะมันไม่ใช่สิ่งที่เราฝัน หรือแท้จริงแล้วตัวเรากำลังมองมันด้วย “เลนส์“ ที่บดบังสายตาเราอยู่ ? 😶‍🌫️⋆ﾟ＊

⋮ ⌗ ┆🎼 “ครูกรีน“ นิธิวัชร์ ตันติภัสร์สิริ 𝄞˚₊‧
 ครูสอนร้องเพลงและการพูด ผู้ที่เคยตามล่าความฝันการประกวดร้องเพลงในรายการที่นับว่ายิ่งใหญ่ที่สุดในประเทศอย่าง Academy Fantasia หรือ AF แต่ชีวิตก็เปลี่ยนผันจนทำให้เขาได้มาทำอาชีพอันใหญ่ยิ่งที่เรียกว่า “ครู“ 🧑🏻‍🏫🦯˚₊

 ⋆ ִֶָ˖·˳˖🛋️จากความอคติกับสิ่งที่โลกบังคับให้เราเป็น สุดท้ายเราจะมีวิธีการหาจุดเปลี่ยน ให้ชีวิตมีความสุขกับจุดที่เรายืนอยู่ได้อย่างไร ˚₊· ➳❥ Nitiwat “Kru Green AF7” Tantipatsiri is the founder of The Modern Melody Music Studio, where he teaches music, singing, public speaking, and communication. He develops speaking curricula by integrating Acting, Vocal Training, and Communication to help learners build confidence from within, organize their thoughts, and express themselves with authenticity and impact. In his talk, Kru Green looks back on the early years of his teaching career—a path he did not begin with love, but with uncertainty, disappointment, and the need to survive. Through a life-changing encounter with one student, he discovered that the work he once resisted had quietly been creating joy and meaning for others. His talk asks a simple but powerful question: do we truly hate what we do, or are we only seeing it through the wrong lens? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.description:
𓏲 ๋࣭  ࣪ ˖🏮ชีวิตและความตายเป็นเสมือนทางคู่ขนานที่ไม่มีวันบรรจบกัน วันที่ความตายมาถึง ชีวิตก็จะไม่อยู่ตรงนี้แล้ว แต่เหตุการณ์ที่ทำให้เราเข้าใกล้มันมากที่สุดคือการจากไปของคนที่เรารัก 🪦𓂃 𓈒𓏸

‧₊˚ ⋅ 🎙️ “เซย์ริว” เรณุวัชร์ สุนันท์วงศ์ ศิษย์เก่าเตรียมอุดมศึกษา ผู้ประกาศข่าวผู้เชื่อว่าการแลกเปลี่ยนทางความคิด และการพยายามเข้าใจซึ่งกันและกัน จะสามารถช่วยเปลี่ยนแปลงโลกไปในทางที่ดีขึ้น ⚖️⊹ ࣪ ˖

𓍢ִ໋🀦 🎞️ ถ้าเปรียบความตายเป็นภาพง่าย ๆ คงเป็นเหมือนเงาดำที่น่ากลัว แต่ความเป็นจริง ความตายสามารถเป็นสิ่งอื่นที่สะท้อนธรรมชาติของสรรพสิ่งที่สวยงามได้ 🐉⊹ ࣪ ﹏ Renuvajra Sunandavongsa (Seiryu) is a former student of Triam Udom Suksa School. Now, He is a news anchor at TNN16 and an MA student Philosophy. He believes that life and death are like parallell lines which would never meet each other. When death comes, life will not be there. Nevertheless, the incident that we are in the closest position to death is when we have lost someone whom we loved most. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

🕊️“คนเราตายได้เพียงครั้งเดียว” จริงหรือ ?… เราอาจตายไปแล้ว.. มากกว่าหนึ่งครั้งในหนึ่งชีวิต ₊˚⊹

˚⊱🏃🏻‍♀️‍➡️"โนเบล" พัชรนันท์ สุวรรณสกนธ์ นักเรียนเตรียมอุดมศึกษาผู้ตระหนักได้ว่ามนุษย์เรานั้นตายไปแล้วนับครั้งไม่ถ้วน ⏳𓇢𓆸

⋆.˚🌳 เมื่อแม้แต่ต้นไม้ยังผลัดใบเพื่อเปลี่ยนผ่านฤดูกาล มนุษย์ก็ย่อมเปลี่ยนผันไปเช่นเดียวกัน เพราะต้องประสบพบเหตุการณ์หลายหลากตัวตนจึงตายจากและแปรเปลี่ยนไป. . Nobel is a Triamudom student who is always thinking about death. She is trying to figure out why her identity right now isn’t like how she was in the past. The turning point was when she had a chance to be an exchange student in the US. She realized that people always change their identity when they get older or gain new experiences. recentItems.title: Seasoning the soul | Kamares Rithdaychar | TEDxTriam Udom Suksa Youth
recentItems.description:
⊹ ࣪ ˖🍽️ อาหารหนึ่งจาน หลากรสชาติ หลายรสนิยม แม้อาหารที่ขึ้นชื่อว่าอร่อยที่สุด ก็ไม่จำเป็นต้องเป็นอาหารที่ทุกคนชอบที่สุด ♥️˙✧˖

‧₊˚🥨꒷꒦เพราะทุกจาน มีรสและเรื่องราวที่แตกต่างกันออกไปเสมอ ขึ้นอยู่กับการ ‘ปรุง’ โดยวัตถุดิบแห่งประสบการณ์ที่ซ่อนอยู่ 🔍👀୧ ‧₊˚ Kamares “Baitong” Rithdaychar is an alumna of Triam Udom Suksa School, a chef, restaurant owner, and former contestant on Hell’s Kitchen Thailand Season 1. For her, food is more than a craft; it is a way of understanding people, memories, and the many layers of life.

Drawing from her experiences in the kitchen and on the competition stage, Baitong explores how every life, like every dish, is composed of many flavors. Some are sweet, some are bitter, some are difficult to swallow, yet all of them become part of who we are. Her talk reflects on the courage to taste every flavor of life without allowing any single one to define us completely, and asks, “How do we season a meaningful life?” This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The People Your System Fails First | Jackie Chambers de Freitas | TEDxBuckheadAve
recentItems.description:
Thirty years ago, Jackie Chambers de Freitas walked into her first server room and counted. She was the only Black woman there. That experience gave her a perspective she would spend decades learning to understand. Drawing on her career in technology leadership, Jackie challenges a common assumption: the people a system fails first aren't exceptions to dismiss. They may be the most accurate source of information about what isn't working. She reveals why the view from the edge can help us build better systems for everyone. Jackie Chambers de Freitas is VP of AI Delivery & Transformation at Salesforce, where she leads initiatives that turn artificial intelligence into measurable business value. With more than 30 years of experience, she has helped global organizations accelerate innovation, improve efficiency, and drive business results. She spoke at RenderATL 2026 on moving AI beyond prototypes into real-world impact.

A British woman with Jamaican roots and an HBCU alumna, Jackie is passionate about expanding access and opportunity for underrepresented talent. She champions women in technology, mentors emerging leaders, and advocates for purposeful leadership and well-being. She serves on the board of New Voices for Reproductive Justice and was inducted as an Honorary Member of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Inc. in 2024. Her leadership philosophy centers on clarity, inclusion, and creating opportunities for others to succeed. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What our words reveal that our actions cannot | Aadi Jhawar | TEDxKings College School
recentItems.description: Aadi considers the language organisations reach for when they have something difficult to say, and what is lost when a decision is described in terms that make it sound inevitable. Drawing on examples from business, medicine, and sport, he looks at the difference between wording chosen to protect the listener and wording chosen to protect the speaker. Aadi is a Year 11 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon, with a particular passion for science and linguistics. He is fascinated by how scientific discovery helps us understand the world, and by how words across different languages shape the way we communicate with, interact with, and respect others. Beyond the classroom, he plays cricket and racquet sports, and nurtures his love of music through the piano and violin. He also follows Formula 1 and enjoys designing and racing model cars. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Mistakes and how they shaped the world | Arjun Singh Patnaik | TEDxKings College School
recentItems.description: Arjun looks at a series of discoveries in science and in food that began with something going wrong, from penicillin to polyethylene. His interest is in what the people involved did next, and in why an accident becomes a discovery for some and a wasted afternoon for others. Arjun is a Year 8 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon, who loves Mathematics and Science and is passionate about learning new things. Outside the classroom, he runs a school club with some of his friends. In his free time, he plays squash and cricket, and enjoys reading and the occasional video game. He is also an avid chess player and represents both the school and Surrey at chess. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
